time_saved.caveat: Estimate of the methodic as written, not a product measurement — gauntlet/accepted-gaps.md:24-33 (no runner exists).

scored_criteria.criterion: Every percentage carries its denominator as a separate fact
Figures traceable to the company's own published document, with its year
What the disclosure omits is recorded, with a home in the schema
No named individual below executive level appears anywhere
scored_criteria.note: Passes on the Creator's discipline, not the methodic's — dimensions.ts:31 pushes the other way and conclusions.ts has no naming policy.

scored_criteria.criterion: The counter-case is the company's own best framing, quoted
scored_criteria.note: Reachable and mandatory; no field holds a verbatim attributed quotation.

scored_criteria.criterion: Conclusions are about the structure, never participants' judgement

engine_walk.note: Best fit in the catalogue; the Choosing table at ENGINES.md:162-171 would not route an arithmetic-led document topic here.
Safest for an audience currently inside the subject — ENGINES.md:62-63 never tells the viewer they were wrong. Catalogue gives no signal of this.
No competing explanations; forcing it would trip the D-rigged tells.
Excellent on the morning a new vintage drops, poor for 51 weeks. No notion of a recurring news peg.

Rank ladder is naturally ordered difficulty and the rungs are joined by BUT — but F wins density by discarding the derivation (the product), and its witnessed affect is comic over rungs that are cohorts of real people. Unrecordable: engine_fit.fit is one scalar.

hypothesis_responses.lead: HYPOTHESIS 1 — the seven columns are market-shaped and will collapse or leave orphans
hypothesis_responses.detail: 6/7 held without stretching; flows and politics were the two strongest fits. The defect is not the column shape but that RESEARCH-PROMPT.md:21-22 scopes its table honestly ('For a market/economics topic') while dimensions.ts:1-5 universalises it and dimensions.ts:7-14 closes the union so no other set can exist. Filed as finding 04.

hypothesis_responses.lead: HYPOTHESIS 2 — the MEASURED/OBSERVED/INFERRED/ASSUMED ladder has no honest rung for interpretive evidence
hypothesis_responses.detail: There is no such ladder in the research methodic. It appears only in pipeline/DIRECTOR-DIMENSION.md:9, a document that states at :3-5 that nothing in it is implemented, and it labels the repo's own design claims rather than research evidence. A notebook has confidence: high|medium|low (NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md:46-47) and nothing else. The real gap is filed as finding 05.

hypothesis_responses.lead: HYPOTHESIS 3 — the unhinged leap tier is unsafe when a conclusion names a living person
hypothesis_responses.detail: Routing motive to unhinged (conclusions.ts:32-33) plus the mandatory falsifier (:55) and OFF-by-default (:15-16) is the correct guardrail for this beat. The danger is upstream: if an observed omission can only be stated as a conclusion, the strongest evidence inherits a leap and arrives switched off. Fix the fact layer (finding 03) and the ladder is sound.

hypothesis_responses.lead: HYPOTHESIS 4 — Phase 1's mandatory counter-case row is unsatisfiable for topics with no literature
hypothesis_responses.detail: The counter-case is printed in the same document as the primary evidence and is unusually strong. The problem is the opposite: no field holds it verbatim and attributed. Filed as finding 07.

findings.creator: consumer-scam
findings.topic: An MLM income disclosure statement read against three prior vintages and the compensation plan
findings.title: scale_conversions[] carries no back-reference to the fact it converts and no base for the quantity
findings.expected: A scale conversion should name the fact id it derives from and the base of the quantity, so a percentage-to-people conversion is auditable against the source figure it came from.
findings.got: scale_conversions[] is {raw, felt} — two free-text strings. The sibling field analogy_candidates[] is {for, analogy, quality} and DOES bind to what it explains. The one structure in the notebook whose entire job is arithmetic is the only cross-referencing structure that lost its cross-reference.
findings.refuter_note: Not the topic being hard — the topic is one document and long division. A competent execution could not produce this without inventing a field, which env.md:33-35 defines as a notebook-schema finding rather than a workaround. DIRECTOR-DIMENSION.md:399 shows the same design already using supports:[fact-id] one layer downstream, so the pattern is known and was not applied here.
findings.l2_priority: Produce a notebook with three percentage-derived conversions and check whether the rendered script can be traced back to the source figures without reading the researcher's mind.

findings.creator: consumer-scam
findings.topic: An MLM income disclosure statement read against three prior vintages and the compensation plan
findings.title: facts[] cannot carry a quantity, its unit or its denominator as structured data — a percentage and its base survive only as prose
findings.expected: A fact stating a percentage should carry the population it is a percentage of as structured data, so no downstream step can quote the percentage bare.
findings.got: facts[] is {id, claim, load_bearing, source, confidence, as_of, note?}. There is no value, unit, base or population field; a percentage and its base can only co-exist inside one free-text claim, against Rule 1's 'no prose, claims are one line'. Nothing downstream can even detect that a fact contains a number. The loss is demonstrated three times in the shipped incumbent run: notebook.json:139 'in risk-on conditions' -> script--adjudication.md:98-99 drops it; notebook.json:163 '(~2% of supply)' -> script--adjudication.md:46-47 drops the base; notebook.json:113 'MSTR fell ~70%' has no base at all and script--adjudication.md:79 repeats it bare.
findings.refuter_note: The strongest possible refutation — 'a competent researcher would have kept the qualifier' — is disproved by the artifact: the run that DEFINED the methodic dropped three qualifiers between its own notebook and its own script. Secondary: RESEARCH-PROMPT.md:84-85 actively prefers ratios over levels and notebook.json:368 hardens it to 'never a precise figure', which is correct for a moving price and wrong for a figure published once in a filing.
findings.l2_priority: Trace every percentage in the rendered script back to a notebook fact AND its base; count the bare ones.

findings.creator: consumer-scam
findings.topic: An MLM income disclosure statement read against three prior vintages and the compensation plan
findings.title: No fact-level marker for an absence — what a primary document declines to say has no instruction, no marker and no column
findings.expected: A finding of the form 'the primary document does not report X, and the omission is the evidence' should be recordable as positive, marked evidence, hunted for by an explicit instruction, and placed in a column.
findings.got: A negative fact IS expressible as free-text facts[].claim and satisfies Rule 2 (it has a source and a date), so 'there is no home' would be an overstatement. What is absent: (a) any structured marker distinguishing 'the document reports X' from 'the document does not report X' — they are the same shape to every consumer; (b) any instruction to interrogate omissions — all six Phase-1 rows ask what is there, and Phase 7 asks only what the RESEARCHER does not know; (c) a column — an untagged absence-fact hits ?? DEFAULT_DIMENSION and files as a price (G-000). The two fields that sound like homes both invert the polarity: unknowns[].impact is defined as 'what the script may not say', and research_gaps[] is the researcher's own failures.
findings.refuter_note: Deliberately narrowed after the 'present somewhere you did not read' refutation bit. Absence-as-evidence IS blessed at the tension level (RESEARCH-PROMPT.md:48, shape 4 'The absent thing') and produced the incumbent run's best beat (notebook.json:63-70) — so the concept is present and only the fact-level representation is missing. Decisive corroboration: DIRECTOR-DIMENSION.md:156-161 reasons the identical question through for the visual layer, invents negates:true, and states the reason as 'an absence is the visual most likely to be silently dropped by a downstream step that cannot render it'. The design has had this argument, won it, and applied the answer one layer too late. Filed undecided because it converges with public-corruption from a different area; the content-vs-lens ruling is the judge's.
findings.l2_priority: Run a document-led topic and count how many omission findings survive into the script without being reworded as hedges.

findings.creator: consumer-scam
findings.topic: An MLM income disclosure statement read against three prior vintages and the compensation plan
findings.title: One domain table, honestly scoped to markets in the prompt, silently universalised by the board — and the column set is a closed type
findings.expected: A non-market topic should get a domain table for its own shape, or an explicit instruction on how to derive one, and the board should be able to hold the resulting columns.
findings.got: RESEARCH-PROMPT.md:21-22 is correctly scoped ('For a market/economics topic, that is at minimum:') and no second table exists anywhere for any other shape. dimensions.ts:1-5 then adopts those same six as THE review columns for every topic, and dimensions.ts:7-14 makes DimensionId a closed TypeScript union, so a different column set cannot be expressed as data at all. A document-led fraud topic fills 6/7 by luck; its three genuinely orphaned groups (document-construction, documented-omissions, vintage-comparability) cannot be added without a code change, which turns a content-level fix into a mechanism edit.
findings.refuter_note: Partially CONTRADICTS the orchestrator's HYPOTHESIS 1. The columns are not market-shaped in substance — flows and politics were this topic's two strongest fits, and macro was the only empty one. The defect is the missing second table plus the closed union, not the column semantics. Recorded this way deliberately so the judge is not handed a confirmation of the lead it wrote.
findings.l2_priority: Confirm whether an L2 researcher on a non-market topic uses the market table, invents one silently, or reports the absence.

findings.creator: consumer-scam
findings.topic: An MLM income disclosure statement read against three prior vintages and the compensation plan
findings.title: confidence conflates source reliability with source self-interest, and demotes a subject's own legally-required filing to low
findings.expected: A notebook should be able to say that a source is simultaneously the most authoritative artifact available AND written by the interested party — two answers, because they are two questions.
findings.got: facts[] carries one axis: confidence high|medium|low, described as source reliability, with the only self-interest rule being 'Vendor research is low by default' (NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md:47). A company's own income disclosure is vendor research about itself, so the rule stamps low on the primary source of the entire topic — and NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md:45 then declares load-bearing facts at low confidence 'the single most dangerous thing in a notebook', flagging the whole notebook for being correct. There is no evidence-kind axis at all: the MEASURED/OBSERVED/INFERRED/ASSUMED ladder assumed by the gauntlet rubric exists only in DIRECTOR-DIMENSION.md:9, an explicitly unimplemented proposal, where it labels the repo's own design claims rather than research evidence.
findings.refuter_note: CONTRADICTS the premise of HYPOTHESIS 2 rather than the hypothesis: the methodic under test has no evidence ladder to find a rung on. Not present-but-missed — the anti-pattern note at :109 ('laundered confidence') shows the design thought about self-interested sources and resolved it in one direction only, toward demotion.
findings.l2_priority: Check whether a run marks a primary self-published filing high or low, and what the script does with the label either way.

findings.creator: consumer-scam
findings.topic: An MLM income disclosure statement read against three prior vintages and the compensation plan
findings.title: engine_fit.fit is a single scalar — 'structurally excellent, tonally disqualifying' cannot be recorded, and the catalogue has no audience axis
findings.expected: An engine assessment should separate structural fit from register/audience fit, so 'the shape is perfect and the tone would cost me my audience' is recordable and survives to the next session.
findings.got: engine_fit[] is {engine, fit, why, recommended?} with fit as one word. Every entry in the incumbent run judges material shape only ('no second domain to transfer to', 'no news event'). ENGINES.md characterises each engine by 'the viewer's pleasure' and never by what the engine does to a viewer who is inside the subject. Concretely: Engine F (Anchor Ladder) is the best structural description of a rank ladder in the catalogue, and is disqualified here on two grounds it cannot express — it wins density by discarding the derivation (ENGINES.md:132-142), and its witnessed affect is comic over rungs that are, in this topic, cohorts of real people.
findings.refuter_note: Could the why field carry it? Yes as prose, which is exactly the failure mode this schema elsewhere forbids — recommended? is the only machine-readable output and it is a boolean over a two-dimensional judgement. Also a routing point: the Choosing table would not send an arithmetic-led document topic to Engine B, which is its best fit.
findings.l2_priority: Have the run assess all seven engines and see whether any tonal or audience objection survives into engine_fit at all.

findings.creator: consumer-scam
findings.topic: An MLM income disclosure statement read against three prior vintages and the compensation plan
findings.title: No structured home for a verbatim, attributed, dated quotation of the counter-party
findings.expected: When the counter-case is the subject's own published framing, the notebook should hold it as an exact quotation with its source and edition, distinguishable from the researcher's paraphrase.
findings.got: steel_man is {claim, evidence[], statement, why_include} — statement is free prose with no source, no date, no page, no quotation marker. counter_positions_to_state_fairly[] is a bare array of strings, unsourced and undated (notebook.json:354-358). Nothing distinguishes 'their words' from 'my summary of their argument'. In a domain where the letters come from law firms, that distinction is the exposure control.
findings.refuter_note: CONTRADICTS HYPOTHESIS 4 for this topic: the counter-case is not merely reachable, it is co-located with the primary evidence in the same document and is genuinely strong (it attacks the denominator). The steel-man requirement is satisfiable here; the representation is what fails. Note the convergence: the counter-case and the arithmetic are fighting over the same missing field, the denominator (finding 02).
findings.l2_priority: Check whether the steel_man statement in a produced notebook is a quotation or a paraphrase, and whether the script presents it as either.

findings.creator: consumer-scam
findings.topic: An MLM income disclosure statement read against three prior vintages and the compensation plan
findings.title: actors.emptyMeans asserts a defect where a deliberate refusal to name is a safety decision, and no naming policy exists anywhere
findings.expected: An empty or cohort-only actors column should be readable as a deliberate exposure choice, and the methodic should carry a naming rule for domains where the agents are private individuals.
findings.got: dimensions.ts:31 states an empty actors column means 'Nobody is named — the story has no agents', which tells a reviewer they have failed when they have in fact protected a private individual. This Creator's rule — never name anyone below executive level — passes on her own discipline alone: conclusions.ts contains no naming policy despite the lens shape in the skill listing 'conclusion-policy: max leap, falsifier standard, naming rules' as a first-class field.
findings.refuter_note: Tested the emptyMeans as env.md:11-13 instructs — it is a claim about what an empty column signifies, and in this domain the claim is false. Scored minor rather than major because it is a label edit on a column that this topic did fill; the trust_erosion is high but the frequency is low. Expect the two named-living-people seats to hit it harder.
findings.l2_priority: Check whether a produced notebook names any individual below executive level, and whether anything in the methodic would have stopped it.

findings.creator: consumer-scam
findings.topic: An MLM income disclosure statement read against three prior vintages and the compensation plan
findings.title: sources[] cannot identify a document edition, and as_of dates the fact rather than the document vintage
findings.expected: A fact drawn from the 2022 edition of an annually-republished document, read in 2026, should carry the document's vintage as distinct from the date of the claim — because the series across vintages is the finding.
findings.got: sources[] is a flat array of URL strings with no title, publisher, edition or retrieval date (notebook.json:413-427). as_of is defined as the date of the fact and drives currency, not the vintage of the source. For a document republished annually at the same URL, a fact can silently point at next year's PDF, and the three-year comparison this topic is built on is unrepresentable — which is also the third named orphan group, vintage-comparability.
findings.refuter_note: Not solved by currency (NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md:84), which is about OUR shelf life, not the source's internal comparability across editions. Not solved by note?, which is prose. The incumbent topic hid this because price sources are continuous rather than editioned — a topic-specific blind spot in the founding run, which is precisely what this exercise hunts.
findings.l2_priority: Check whether a produced notebook can distinguish two editions of the same document at the same URL.
